title: MIRROR ME — credits and asset sources

entries.title: MIRROR ME — concept, story, house and sound
entries.creator: Skewernet; AI-assisted development with OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex
entries.license: Original project work; no separate asset-license grant
entries.changes: Original game direction, writing, L-shaped house, seamless threshold portal, seven-chapter progression, keepsake puzzles, wake room, funeral-radio geometry, authored props, interface and procedural animation. Layered blood, pools, bedding/shroud forms, knife and care-room evidence in src/revelation.mjs are original project geometry and canvas artwork. Ambience, footsteps, crawling, breaths, sob-like textures, knocks, mechanical sounds and music-box tones are authored Web Audio synthesis; no external sound or prop library. The separate intruder in src/demon.mjs adds an original asymmetric facial sculpt, marbled tissue and ruined-cloth shaders, and layered wet strand hair while reusing the credited MakeHuman base. Its finite nonverbal breath, throat and contact textures are synthesized by project code; no film monster, likeness, chant, sound recording or new external asset is included. The later bathroom-to-bed evidence trail, hall-photograph interaction and wounded funeral-room mother use original project geometry, surface shaders and animation on the credited human rig. The funeral-parlor rebuild adds an open casket, empty seating and a separately generated aged Evelyn character guided by the original family portrait. Her wounded form has removed skin/garment faces, modeled cavities and torn tissue attached to the measured rig; the clean casket form remains intact. The accelerated strike and same-voice Goodnight are original scene direction. The menu/settings redesign, original dual-bell telephone ringer, irregular crawler circuit interruptions, filmic presentation pass and animated handheld flashlight prop are project code and geometry. First-person draw/stow and item-reaching animations are authored against the credited Mara rig; no external animation or prop pack is used. The producer/jam/title splashes, content warning, optional original menu atmosphere, hand/flashlight reflection replay, finite mirror twitches and eye-bleeding shader, kitchen blood-writing and whole-house/funeral electrical blackouts are original code, procedural artwork and sound. Relay banks and reflection rattles are synthesized before play; no film sound or likeness is copied. The later horror pass adds an original hand-traced stroke atlas for finger-smeared blood writing and drips, procedural scorched funeral-parlor surfaces, player-initiated crawler contact/failure animation and the shared slow menu/parlor score in src/dread-score.mjs. Recurring glottal clicks, descending growls and finite attack textures in src/horror-textures.mjs are original deterministic PCM generated before play; no film audio, actor recording or external creature sample is used. The final polish replaces the rotary telephone with original molded-case/dial/cradle/receiver/connected-cord geometry, corrects anatomical flashlight gripping and item reaches, and isolates a restrained asymmetric mirror face/pose from the unchanged normal Mara and creature rigs. Final old-house dressing adds original broken furnishings, scattered papers/plaster, wall/ceiling cracks, torn caution tape and eight pre-baked anatomical wall hands, confined to the late chapter with clear navigation. A single reused crawler supplies four finite post-lamp room glimpses. The funeral adds a collision-validated simulation-clock survey, aisle approach and held casket gaze before the established report, accusation and Goodnight strike.

entries.title: Kokoro-82M v1.0 — synthetic dialogue
entries.creator: Kokoro / hexgrad; ONNX conversion and runtime by k2-fsa / sherpa-onnx; original dialogue by MIRROR ME
entries.license: Engine and model weights: Apache-2.0; dialogue: original project writing
entries.changes: Forty-three original takes synthesized offline: forty-one narrative/broken-word performances, one ambient kitchen weather bulletin and one finite fictional funeral news report. Mara and the glass: bf_emma; Mum: bf_isabella; both radio readers: bm_george. All three Mum calls use telephone bandwidth; the second pleads through seven uneven phrases and the third directs the diary and reverse-sound order. The final Mum lines use clear full-range speech. The broken-word take uses scripted phrase spacing and restrained amplitude modulation; it is not a recorded human sob. Three additional clock-chapter mirror hints connect clock hands, bathwater and Mum without stating the time or the next action. Telephone/radio filtering, original layered low/raspy glass treatment with glottal clicks across all fifteen glass takes, spatial playback and loudness/headroom mastering are project work. No film audio or actor performance is sampled. Only the weather loop has a padded quiet tail; the funeral report plays once. Supplied synthetic presets; no human actor performance or real-person voice clone is claimed. One additional full-range disembodied lamp reminder uses the established bf_isabella Mum preset, with three measured phrase captions and a quiet airy treatment. The previous forty-two takes and their hashes remain unchanged.

entries.title: MakeHuman / MPFB — female base, morphology and game rig
entries.creator: MakeHuman Team — Data Collection AB, Joel Palmius and Jonas Hauquier
entries.changes: Adult female morphological blend at 1.74 m; helper removal, anatomical subdivision, resting pose and glTF export. MPFB mouth-opening expression added as a jaw morph; the CC0 inside-mouth texture is copied unmodified as inside-mouth-mask.jpg. The project adds distance-driven foot planting, measured-bind-axis limb solving, crawling/ceiling poses and anatomical horror deformation. The existing credited rig is also reused for the seated wake figures and covered adult hand in the revealed room; no new body or monster model is downloaded. Evelyn is a separate 1.62 m, 68-year-old character built independently from the CC0 morphology, with different aged face/body proportions and a separately exported 53-bone asset. Her clean casket pose and bone-attached wounded variant never load or modify Mara’s GLB. Build parameters and source checksums are in evelyn.json and evelyn-sources.json. The first-person body reuses an independent instance of Mara with private head/neck geometry removal, natural walking, measured arm solving, posed grip fingers and draw/stow/reach animation. Other character and reflection geometry/materials remain independent.

entries.title: MakeHuman — system skin, eyes, hair, clothing and shoes
entries.creator: MakeHuman Team — Data Collection AB, Joel Palmius and Jonas Hauquier
entries.changes: System skin, detailed eyes, bob hairstyle, brows, lashes, casual clothing and shoes03 black shoes fitted to the female character; chestnut hair tint, PBR tuning, authored blood/material variants and desaturated mourning clothes. The clothed mesh and skeleton are reused for crawling and distorted figures, seated mourners and the covered adult hand; those poses and variants are project-authored, not separately downloaded assets. Evelyn uses the separate old female skin, short waved hairstyle, fitted elegant blouse/skirt and shoes04 system assets; her portrait-inspired floral fabric, aging choices and physical injury geometry are original project work.

entries.title: Original generated family images, material atlases and wound decal
entries.creator: Created for MIRROR ME with OpenAI image generation
entries.license: Original project artwork; no third-party asset-license grant
entries.changes: Original AI-generated fictional family images and house material artwork. Current tactile atlas supplies wallpaper, plaster and painted-panel albedos through quadrant crops; framed photos sample the family atlas. The earlier house atlas remains recorded. Generated artwork, not photographic capture. The intruder's original RGBA torn-tissue decal was generated for this project and projected onto its facial sculpt. Its generation brief and exact output hash are recorded in assets/character/unkept-wound.json; no existing film face, likeness or wound asset is used.

entries.title: Original Mara title-mirror render plates
entries.creator: MIRROR ME — in-engine rendering of the credited Mara rig and house
entries.license: Original project renders; underlying assets retain their credited CC0 / CC BY 4.0 licenses
entries.changes: Offline WebP renders use the existing MakeHuman/MPFB Mara model, its authored mirror-distortion state and the existing house. The two character plates retain transparency and matching framing; a dim hallway plate supplies reflection depth. The hallway includes the separately credited Eric Chadwick / Wayfair wood maps (CC BY 4.0), Poly Haven lighting/materials and original house surfaces. Source assets and their licenses remain credited above. Camera recipe and input/output hashes are in menu-mara-sources.json. Original SVG fractures, chipped glass, displaced shards and finite menu glimpses are project presentation code. No extra runtime renderer, new human model or new external artwork is included. The distorted title plate is refreshed from the refined asymmetric mirror face/pose; the normal Mara and hallway plates retain their established framing.

entries.title: Skewer Games — supplied logo and Skewer Blade splash font
entries.creator: Skewer Games; supplied by Skewernet
entries.license: User-supplied project branding; no separate asset-license grant
entries.changes: Approved transparent studio PNG copied byte-for-byte from the supplied SkewerGames-LogoMatched-Source.zip. Skewer Blade Regular Version 0.20 converted losslessly from the supplied SkewerBlade-Regular.ttf to local WOFF2 with fontTools; all outlines, metrics, names, character mappings, kerning and ligatures retained. Logo appears on the producer splash; the display font is scoped to splash headings. Readable body/UI fonts and the established main-menu typography remain. Upload and output hashes are recorded in skewer-brand-sources.json. These owner-provided identity assets have no separate redistribution license supplied; no open-source license is inferred.
